..One of the things I appreciate about the Sonoran 
Desert here in Southeast Arizona is that on a breezy day, you 
can hear the wind whisper as it moves through the needles of the
palo verde, stalks of the ocotillo and thorns along the spines 
of stately saguaros. Unfortunately, the next few days will not 
offer a gentle whisper. Mother Nature is about to clear its 
throat, and when it does, we could be looking at one of the more
significant easterly wind event Southeast Arizona has 
experienced in quite some time. 

The upper pattern this morning is defined by an upper low over
northern Colorado with a trough axis extending to the WSW into 
Western Arizona, and a high amplitude ridge off the West coast
(mainly along 128W) with the northern portions of the ridge axis
flopping into the Pacific Northwest. The latest water vapor
imagery indicated a shortwave diving south into the mean trough
along the eastern periphery of the upper ridge, with aspirations
to carve out a closed-low over the SW Arizona by 16/00Z this
afternoon. 

The building ridge in the northwest will drive an anomalously 
strong surface high southward through the Intermountain West and
into the southern Rockies by this evening. That closed upper- 
low will help pull this strong surface high westward into 
Southeast Arizona tonight into Friday. The ensemble members of 
the GFS and ECMWF remain consistent with the evolution of this 
solution over the past several days, with little variance. The 
15/00Z GFS and ECMWF ensemble runs still indicate the surface 
high will be 3.5 to 4.5 standard deviations above the norm along
the SE AZ/SW NM border by 16/21Z Friday afternoon. 

Model guidance continues to indicate 850 mb winds between 45-55
kts across our CWA between 16/06Z Friday morning thru 17/06Z 
Friday evening, with winds remaining elevated between 35-45 kts 
through 17/18Z Saturday. This prolonged period of strong easterly
flow, combined with a very tight surface pressure gradient
maintain the high confidence we will see a significant and 
potentially long-duration wind event across Southeast Arizona. 

The 15/00Z GFS deterministic model still indicated strong 
static stability near and immediately above ridge-top level. 
This, combined with the persistent strong easterly cross-barrier
flow appears favorable for mountain-wave development...with 
potentially significant downslope wind acceleration along the 
lee slopes of the higher terrain (west to northwest side of the
higher terrain in this particular case). 

This is not the typical wind event we see impacting Southeast 
Arizona. This one will be significant due to the stable air just
above the mountains funneling the winds back down the leeward 
side of the terrain. In fact, to support this idea, both the 
15/00Z HREF and REFS indicate a 50-80% probability of winds in 
excess of 70 mph hugging locations immediately to the W/NW of 
the higher terrain. This scenario may result in sustained 
damaging winds to the aforementioned locations and should be 
taken very seriously. We have been trying to get the word out 
that this is an anomalously strong event, encouraging those with 
wind-vulnerable property to take the necessary precautions and 
secure their items. Although the strongest winds may be focused
immediately downstream of the higher terrain, terrain gaps and 
east-west oriented valleys will also be susceptible to strong 
winds given the magnitude and duration of the low-level pressure
gradient.

A High Wind Warning is in effect from 11 PM MST this evening 
through 11 PM MST Friday from central Pima County eastward. A 
Wind Advisory will then be in effect from 11 PM MST Friday 
through 2 PM MST Saturday afternoon. Expect east to southeast
winds 30-45 mph with gusts 50-70 mph. These winds could lead to
downed trees and power poles as well as areas of blowing dust. 
High profile vehicles should also exercise caution when driving
in strong cross-winds.
